questions.stem: Why do most metals need to be extracted from ores?

options.text: Because metals are always found as pure elements
Because most metals are too reactive to exist naturally as pure elements and are found combined with other elements in compounds
Because metals are only found dissolved in water
Because metals need to be cleaned before use

questions.explanation: Most metals are reactive enough to combine with other elements, so they are found in the Earth's crust as compounds in ores. They must be extracted (separated from the other elements) before they can be used.

options.text: A pure sample of metal
A rock containing enough metal or metal compound to make extraction worthwhile
A type of alloy
A metal that has been recycled

questions.explanation: An ore is a naturally occurring rock that contains a metal or metal compound in sufficient quantities to make it economically worthwhile to extract the metal.

questions.stem: How does the reactivity of a metal determine its extraction method?

options.text: More reactive metals are extracted by heating with carbon; less reactive metals by electrolysis
All metals are extracted the same way
Metals more reactive than carbon are extracted by electrolysis; metals less reactive than carbon are extracted by reduction with carbon
Metals are always extracted by heating their ores in air

questions.explanation: Metals above carbon in the reactivity series (like aluminium and sodium) are too reactive to be reduced by carbon and must be extracted by electrolysis. Metals below carbon (like iron and zinc) can be extracted more cheaply by reduction with carbon.

questions.stem: Why is electrolysis more expensive than reduction with carbon?

options.text: Because electrolysis uses less energy
Because electrolysis requires large amounts of electrical energy to melt the compound and decompose it
Because carbon is very rare and expensive
Because electrolysis produces less metal

questions.explanation: Electrolysis is expensive because it requires a continuous supply of electrical energy. The ionic compound must first be melted (which requires high temperatures) and then the current must be maintained to decompose it into its elements.

questions.stem: Why are gold and platinum found native (as pure metals) in the Earth's crust?

options.text: Because they are very common metals
Because they are so unreactive that they do not combine with other elements
Because they have been purified by natural processes
Because they have very low melting points

questions.explanation: Gold and platinum are at the very bottom of the reactivity series. They are so unreactive that they do not form compounds with other elements, so they exist naturally as pure (native) metals.

questions.stem: Which of the following metals must be extracted using electrolysis?

options.text: Iron
Copper
Aluminium
Lead

questions.explanation: Aluminium is above carbon in the reactivity series, so it cannot be reduced by carbon. It must be extracted using electrolysis. Iron, copper, and lead are below carbon and can be extracted by reduction with carbon.

questions.stem: What does 'reduction' mean in the context of metal extraction?

options.text: Making the metal smaller
Removing oxygen from the metal oxide to obtain the pure metal
Adding oxygen to the metal
Dissolving the metal in acid

questions.explanation: In metal extraction, reduction means removing oxygen from the metal oxide to produce the pure metal. The metal oxide loses oxygen (is reduced) while the reducing agent (like carbon) gains oxygen (is oxidised).
